make.name: Ford
make.description: American carmaker founded by Henry Ford in 1903. Its battery-electric range centres on the Mustang Mach-E, the E-Transit vans and, in Europe, the MEB-based Explorer and Capri plus the Puma Gen-E; the F-150 Lightning EV ended in December 2025 and a low-cost midsize pickup, the Fathom, is due in 2027.

models.name: Mustang Mach-E
models.description: Ford's first purpose-built electric crossover, revealed in November 2019 and on sale since December 2020 as a 2021 model, built in Cuautitlan, Mexico (and by Changan Ford in China until 2025). The 2024 model year brought new motors and more torque across the range plus the Rally; for 2027 the standard-range pack was dropped and every version uses the 88 or 91 kWh pack.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: One body since launch. Hardware changed twice without a restyle: new drive units and higher torque for 2024 (Rally added), and the extended-range pack made standard for 2027.

models.name: F-150 Lightning
models.description: Battery-electric version of the F-150 full-size pickup, built at the Rouge Electric Vehicle Center in Dearborn from April 2022. Ford ended production of the all-electric truck in December 2025 (2025 was the last model year); the next F-150 Lightning is an extended-range EV with a gasoline generator, so it is not a battery-electric vehicle.

generations.name: First generation

models.name: E-Transit
models.description: Battery-electric version of the full-size Transit van, built at Kansas City Assembly for North America from November 2021 and by Ford Otosan in Turkey for Europe from 2022. Sold as a cargo van, chassis cab and cutaway; a larger pack replaced the original 68 kWh battery in the US from 2024-2025.

legacy_notes.note: F-150 Lightning Pro: standard-range truck. Legacy $49,995 price, 150 kW DC and 4.5 s 0-60 are unsourced; 2022 EPA was 230 mi, 2023-2025 240 mi. The truck is no longer built (production ended Dec 2025).

Mach-E GT: legacy price $36,495 and 320 mi range are wrong (GT is EPA 270-280 mi; 2026 MSRP $53,395). 3.3 s 0-60 applies only with the 2024+ Performance Upgrade. Mapped to the current GT variant; legacy image shows a 2021-2023 GT Performance Edition, same body.
Mach-E Select: $42,995 / 250 mi matches the 2024 Select RWD standard-range launch spec; 2026 Select RWD was $37,795 and 260 mi, and the standard-range pack was dropped for 2027.
Mach-E Premium: a trim of the same standard-range RWD hardware as row 41 (duplicate config); claimed on that variant. Premium also came with the extended-range pack.
Mach-E California Route 1: 312 mi matches the 2022-2023 eAWD version (the 2021-2022 RWD version was 305/314 mi). Trim was dropped after 2023; legacy price $56,995 unsourced.
F-150 Lightning Platinum: legacy 320 mi and $49,995 are wrong; Platinum is EPA 300 mi (extended-range pack on 22-inch wheels). Discontinued Dec 2025.

F-150 Lightning Lariat: legacy 230 mi matches the 2022 standard-range rating; $39,974 was the 2022 Pro launch price, not Lariat. Claimed on the standard-range variant (Lariat was also sold with the extended-range pack).
F-150 Lightning XLT: same as row 50 (standard-range, 2022 EPA 230 mi; price is the Pro launch price). Claimed on the standard-range variant.

gaps: Web search budget for the session ran out mid-research; European and Chinese figures come from Ford Germany/UK price lists and Wikipedia fetched directly.
Mach-E 2027 EPA ranges not yet published; 2027 offerings carry price only. 2022-2025 MSRPs not sourced except 2022 (Electrek Oct 2021 guide).
Mach-E 2023 LFP standard-range RWD (EPA 250 mi) not modelled separately; 2021-2023 battery given as gross pack (75.7/98.8 kWh); Ford quoted 68/88 kWh usable for 2021 and 70/91 for 2022.
Mach-E 2024+ 0-60 times only sourced for GT (3.8 s; 3.3 s with Performance Upgrade); DC kW for 2024+ not sourced per variant.
Mach-E connector for 2026-2027 US models not confirmed (CCS1 with NACS adapter through 2025 per Wikipedia).
F-150 Lightning MSRPs (any year) and standard-range DC rate / 0-60 not sourced; Flash and 2025 'ER2' (EPA 300 mi) configurations not split out.

E-Transit US ranges are Ford estimates on the EPA MCT method (not EPA labels); US prices not stated with destination basis, omitted. Europe 96 kWh pack: Ford Germany says 96 kWh usable from 2025/26; earlier 2025 reports said 89 kWh.

Explorer EV and Capri: Ford's 2026 price lists label the RWD Extended Range pack 79 kWh and AWD 77 kWh, the reverse of the 2025 lists (RWD 77, AWD 79); the 2025 values are used. Explorer 0-100 and Capri 58 kWh performance not sourced.
Capri/Explorer UK WLTP ranges are published in miles only; EU (km) figures used instead.
Puma Gen-E: Ford lists 46.8 kWh usable (53 kWh installed) in 2026; Wikipedia gives 43.6 kWh usable / 376 km at launch. Launch-spec variant not split out.

E-Transit Custom / E-Tourneo Custom 2024-2025 battery (64 or 74 kWh usable, sources conflict) not modelled; only the 70 kWh 2026-27 configurations are listed. E-Tourneo Custom WLTP per variant not sourced (Ford page: 273-365 km).
E-Transit Courier and E-Tourneo Courier launch dates not sourced; no Commons image found for the E-Transit Courier or Bronco New Energy.
Territory EV range was rated on NEDC (360 km), which the schema does not accept; price not recorded.
Ranger EV EPA ranges (1999-2001, 50-65 mi) could not be mapped to lead-acid vs NiMH, so omitted.

Power and torque quoted by Ford Europe in kW/PS and Nm were converted to hp and lb-ft (1 kW = 1.341 hp, 1 Nm = 0.7376 lb-ft); top speeds use Ford UK mph figures where given. Ranges and prices are never converted.
Explorer/Capri DC rates: 2025 Ford data gives 135 kW for Extended Range RWD, 2026 UK data 183 kW; left null for that variant.
Transit Connect Electric price ($57,400, 2010) not recorded because its destination basis is unknown.

Not modelled: Ford Th!nk City (1999-2002, sold under the Th!nk brand), Explorer USPS Electric (2001-2002 fleet), JMC-built E-Transit (China), the two Renault Ampere-based small Ford EVs announced Dec 2025 for 2028 (unnamed), and the cancelled three-row electric SUVs (Aug 2024, never named).
